fr.name: French
fr.register: International French. Address the reader as "vous". French typography: non-breaking space before : ; ? ! and inside « guillemets ».

es.name: Spanish
es.register: Neutral Latin American Spanish that also reads naturally in Spain. Address the reader as "usted", warmly. Avoid regionalisms.

de.name: German
de.register: Standard German that reads naturally in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Address the reader as "Sie", warmly and never stiffly. German quotation marks „…“.

it.name: Italian
it.register: Standard Italian. Address the reader with the courteous "Lei", but warmly; avoid bureaucratic phrasing.

ja.name: Japanese
ja.register: Natural Japanese for travellers from Japan, in polite です/ます style: warm and gracious, never stiff or overly formal. Japanese punctuation (、。「」). Names on the keep-in-English list stay in Latin letters.

ko.name: Korean
ko.register: Natural, polite Korean (합니다/해요 as fits a warm hospitality business), clear and friendly, never stiff. Names on the keep-in-English list stay in Latin letters.

zh.name: Simplified Chinese
zh.register: Simplified Chinese for readers from mainland China: warm, polished and natural, never a word-for-word rendering. Full-width Chinese punctuation (，。：“”). Names on the keep-in-English list stay in Latin letters.

hi.name: Hindi
hi.register: Natural, warm standard Hindi in Devanagari, addressing the reader with the respectful आप. Everyday English loanwords that Hindi speakers actually use (session, photo, booking) may stay as they are, written in Devanagari. Use Western digits (0-9), never Devanagari numerals. Names on the keep-in-English list stay in Latin letters.
